brief: Goldman's weekly US wrap frames the September jobs report (29k net adds, unemployment up to 4.2%, prior months revised lower) as 'bad is good': the weakness let GS economists push the expected Fed funds rate hike from October to December, citing lower core PCE inflation. GS's own underlying job-growth estimate is 51k, near breakeven, arguing the headline overstates weakness. Separately, ISM Manufacturing was roughly unchanged (PMI revised down) while construction spending beat, lifting GS's Q3 GDP tracker to +3.4%, a stronger-growth signal alongside soft jobs. Three conundrums get analyst takes: rates keep rising despite cooling inflation because technicals and positioning, not fundamentals, are driving the move (Marshall), though valuation and positioning imply eventual downside absent a catalyst, and capital demand from governments and private markets adds further upward pressure; oil stays elevated even as a doubling of Persian Gulf exports leaves the global market roughly balanced, with GS still wary of escalation risk to energy infrastructure; and capital-markets activity has slowed under higher rates, though Blostein sees a private-equity monetization opportunity ahead as that pressure eases.
